ut_pocket_rocks.blurb: Pocket Rocks is a small sport crag on the hills west of Cedar City, on welded tuff with a sharp, textured feel. It holds about two dozen routes, nearly all bolted, plus a few trad lines and a single top rope. Grades run from easy 5.6 up to 5.11, with the bulk sitting in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, so it suits intermediate climbers best while still offering a handful of moderates. Lines are short, around 60 feet, so a modest rope and a light rack of quickdraws will do. The walls face south: pleasant on cool days, but baking in summer heat. A trail leads from the road up to the base.

ut_choss_cave_2.blurb: Choss Cave is a steep, overhanging cave in Mill Canyon, a quiet side drainage of Echo Canyon in the Wasatch Back. All of its roughly two dozen routes are bolted sport lines on cobbles, short and powerful, with plenty of link-ups between them. This is hard-climber terrain: a single route in the low 5.11s, several at 5.12, and most of the rest in the 5.13 range. The cave has been cleaned up and is mostly solid, though a hold can still snap off. It lies in the shade from mid-afternoon on, which helps on warm days. Expect a walk of about twenty minutes up the drainage, then a short climb to the cave.

ut_damascus_gate_the.blurb: The Damascus Gate is one of the larger sport crags in Maple Canyon's Right Fork in central Utah. A steep, slightly overhanging wall with a prominent prow rising above the pines, it carries about two dozen bolted routes split between two sections. The climbing is aimed at strong sport climbers: a couple of lines in the 5.10 range, a handful of 5.11s, and a big majority in the 5.12 grades, with one 5.13 at the top end. Reach it on foot by heading up the Right Fork trail, the same way as for the Pipe Dream cave; the wall shows up on your left where the canyon tightens.
